title: How scientists in Boston are using AI to decipher the secret language of rats
key_facts: Scientists in the Boston area use microphones, thermal cameras and AI to try to decipher rat communication.
Microphone boxes are placed around Boston, such as near dumpsters, to record high-pitched rat calls.
Human sounds picked up are redacted and deleted for privacy before the audio goes to AI models.
Nick Jourjine of Basis Research Institute: the start is matching what animals do with what they say.
Ricky Meinke of the Rat City Arts Festival hopes call data could help time bait placement so poison boxes are on streets for less time.
No findings about what the calls mean are reported.
quote_evidence: The group places microphone boxes in strategic areas around Boston, such as dumpsters, to record the high-pitched vocalization rats make when communicating.
"That's the start, just trying to match up what animals do with what they say," Jourjine said.
why_it_matters_hint: Understanding rat calls could allow more targeted pest control, but the work is at an early stage.
